content:
Apple has finally responded to soaring memory and other component costs, and pulled no punches. Some increases are over 50%, while memory and storage upgrades double in price in some cases.

These higher prices are likely to persist for years to come, and may never come back down…

9to5Mac readers were already skeptical that Apple would drop prices once component shortages eased. Over two-thirds of those polled expected the price hikes to be permanent.

An analyst report subsequently indicated that supply chain pricing would not see any significant improvement until 2028, and even then, any relief would be modest. Pricing far above historical levels will remain for at least several years, and very likely forever.

If this is indeed the case, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same pace? Will you buy fewer Apple products, or less often? Or will you take other measures, like choosing lower-tier models, buying refurbished, or waiting for sales?

Take our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, in case you plan to change your buying habits in more than one way.
